walkthrough: We have a large sample of $n = 250$ children with bicycle ownership probability $p = 0.65$. We approximate the binomial distribution $X \sim \mathrm{B}(250, 0.65)$ with a continuous normal distribution.

Step 1: Calculate the mean $\mu$ and variance $\sigma^2$:
$$\mu = np = 250 \times 0.65 = 162.5$$
$$\sigma^2 = np(1 - p) = 250 \times 0.65 \times 0.35 = 56.875$$
$$\sigma = \sqrt{56.875} \approx 7.5416$$
Check validity: $np = 162.5 > 5$ and $n(1 - p) = 87.5 > 5$, confirming the normal approximation $Y \sim \mathrm{N}(162.5, 56.875)$ is justified.

Step 2: Apply the continuity correction.
We want 'fewer than 179 children', which means $X \le 178$.
The discrete bar for 178 ends at the continuous boundary $178.5$, so:
$$\mathrm{P}(X < 179) = \mathrm{P}(X \le 178) \approx \mathrm{P}(Y < 178.5)$$
